segments.title: The Ripon II's redesigned engine installation
segments.summary: The Ripon II was so extensively revised around its engine and cooling system that it barely resembled the earlier Ripon I.
segments.body: The Ripon II's nose enclosed a 570-horsepower Napier Lion engine in fitted cowlings. Removing the earlier nose-mounted radiator and its shutters gave the nose a pointed profile. The spinner of a larger two-bladed wooden airscrew emphasized that shape. Cooling came from quadrant-shaped retractable radiators behind the engine bay, which the pilot could extend from both sides of the fuselage.

evidence.note: The transcript contrasts the Ripon II with the earlier aircraft and describes its Napier Lion installation, cowlings, propeller, and retractable side radiators.

segments.title: The Ripon II's undercarriage and torpedo clearance
segments.summary: The Ripon II combined a larger balanced rudder with a new bent-axle undercarriage that left room beneath the fuselage for a torpedo.
segments.body: The Ripon II had a taller balanced rudder with substantially more area than its predecessor. Its new undercarriage used a bent axle on each side, attached to the lower longerons. This left space beneath the fuselage for the torpedo. Telescopic oleo-pneumatic legs extended to fittings at the outboard ends of the lower centre-section front spar.

evidence.note: The transcript describes the enlarged rudder, the redesigned bent-axle undercarriage, its oleo-pneumatic legs, and the clearance left for a torpedo.

segments.title: The Ripon II's structure and folding wings
segments.summary: The Ripon II retained a mixed steel-and-wood fuselage stressed for catapult launches and Blackburn's established folding-wing arrangement for shipboard use.
segments.body: Beneath its refined exterior, the Ripon II retained the basic fuselage structure of its predecessors, stressed for catapult launches. It comprised three detachable units: a steel engine mounting, a steel-tube centre structure, and a tie-rod-braced wooden rear fuselage. The swept-back single-bay wings combined spruce spars and ribs with metal compression struts. Steel interplane struts sat inside streamlined fairings. For shipboard stowage, hinges on the rear spars of the upper and lower centre sections allowed the wings to fold aft, as on earlier Blackburn shipborne aircraft. Ailerons on all four wings followed Blackburn's standard practice.

evidence.note: The transcript describes the inherited fuselage structure, composite wing construction, and wings folding back like earlier Blackburn shipborne aircraft.

segments.title: The Ripon II's fuel system for fourteen-hour reconnaissance
segments.summary: The Ripon II placed its main fuel tank at the centre of gravity and could trade armament for an auxiliary tank that extended reconnaissance endurance to fourteen hours.
segments.body: The Ripon II carried a 145-gallon main fuel tank at the centre of gravity in the central fuselage and pumped fuel onward to a 17-gallon service tank. A separate four-gallon coolant tank sat beside the service tank in the upper centre section. For reconnaissance duties, removing the armament allowed a 120-gallon auxiliary fuel tank to hang from the torpedo crutches, increasing endurance to fourteen hours. A wind-driven pump in the auxiliary tank's nose fed fuel into the main system.

evidence.note: The transcript locates the fuel and coolant tanks and explains that an auxiliary tank on the torpedo crutches could raise reconnaissance endurance to fourteen hours.
